applicability: Valid for positive integer p>q, positive integer multiplier, positive integer bound (capped at 200 to keep the O(bound^3) search tractable), and a positive numeric tolerance. Rejects malformed inputs, booleans, non-positive values, p<=q, and cases where no triple matches within the bound. Intended for small bounded instances of the cube-root identity family; not a symbolic proof and not suitable for large bounds.
description: Searches all positive integer triples (a,b,c) up to the given bound, computing the left side m*sqrt(cbrt(p)-cbrt(q)) and the right side cbrt(a)+cbrt(b)-cbrt(c) in double precision, and returns the minimal sum a+b+c among triples whose difference is below the supplied tolerance. The search is exhaustive over the bounded cube, so it is deterministic; uncertainty comes from floating-point rounding and from the possibility that the true triple lies outside the bound or that multiple near-matches exist.
